title: HA number-theory campaign definition and representation freeze v1
authority: planning-and-audit-only; this manifest grants no parser, kernel, definition, or theorem authority

classification_vocabulary.frozen-compatible: The exact current expansion is accepted as the campaign relation; API completeness is recorded separately.
classification_vocabulary.bridge-required: The exact current expansion remains conservative and usable, but a checked theorem must connect it to the campaign's preferred canonical presentation.
classification_vocabulary.legacy-late: The relation remains usable after its dependencies, but it is quarantined from the foundational K3 data representation because its construction route would be circular with CRT.

arithmetic_axioms.PA2: forall x y. S x = S y -> x = y
arithmetic_axioms.PA4: forall x y. x + S y = S (x + y)
arithmetic_axioms.PA6: forall x y. x * S y = x * y + x

kernel.induction: Ind stores one concrete object-language motive and checks its zero instance and universally quantified successor step before inferring its universal closure.
kernel.cut: Cut checks its lemma in the surrounding context once and checks its body under that proposition; it is proof sharing, not an arithmetic axiom.

definition_boundary.expansion_contract: Every recognized call is hygienically instantiated from a parsed de Bruijn template and returns an ordinary core Formula before tactic elaboration and kernel checking.
definition_boundary.api_authority: Only separately replayed object-level theorem certificates establish introduction, elimination, functionality, decidability, transport, or bridge properties.

definitions.name: Le
definitions.reason: This is the campaign's witness-defined non-strict order and is also the expansion of the <= parser surface.

definitions.name: Lt
definitions.exact_expanded_template: exists h. h + S a = b
definitions.reason: This is the strict witness order used by current bounded arithmetic and by the campaign's canonical bounds.

definitions.name: Dvd
definitions.reason: This is exactly the campaign's base-language divisibility template.

definitions.name: DivRem
definitions.exact_expanded_template: n = d * q + r /\ exists h. h + S r = d
definitions.reason: The relation directly states the canonical quotient/remainder equation and strict remainder bound; totality requires a nonzero divisor and functionality is a theorem.

definitions.name: IsGCD
definitions.exact_expanded_template: ((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall d. (exists u. a = d * u) -> (exists v. b = d * v) -> exists w. g = d * w
definitions.reason: The greatest-common-divisor relation has a unique natural output and requires no primitive gcd function in the core language.

definitions.name: Coprime
definitions.exact_expanded_template: forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1
definitions.reason: The common-divisor definition is constructive and already has checked bridges to IsGCD(1,a,b).

definitions.name: ModEq
definitions.exact_expanded_template: exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v
definitions.reason: This is the campaign's allowed subtraction-free congruence relation, but the preferred post-division presentation is equality of canonical remainders.

required_bridge_theorems.statement_shape: If DivRem(a,m,qa,ra) and DivRem(b,m,qb,rb), then ModEq(m,a,b) iff ra = rb; no separate m != 0 premise is needed because either strict remainder bound rules out m = 0.

definitions.name: Prime
definitions.exact_expanded_template: ~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1
definitions.reason: The current factor-pair definition is constructive, but the campaign freezes its public canonical presentation as p > 1 plus a bounded divisor characterization.

required_bridge_theorems.statement_shape: Prime(p) iff Lt(1,p) and every d with Le(d,p) and Dvd(d,p) satisfies d = 1 or d = p.

definitions.name: BalancedBezout
definitions.exact_expanded_template: exists xp yp xn yn. a * xp + b * yp = d + (a * xn + b * yn)
definitions.reason: Four natural witnesses avoid subtraction and already support checked Bezout arithmetic, but they are not a canonical signed-integer code with a no-negative-zero invariant.

required_bridge_theorems.statement_shape: BalancedBezout witnesses decode to signed coefficients X,Y satisfying a*X+b*Y=d.
Canonical signed coefficients X,Y satisfying a*X+b*Y=d produce four natural BalancedBezout witnesses.
